chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, all from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyas, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'If you are able to not be known (by people), then do so. And what is upon you if people do not praise you? And what is upon you if you are condemned by people while you are praised by Allah?'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'My father, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), said: There is no goodness in life except for two men: a man who increases in goodness every day, and a man who makes up for his death/evil deeds with repentance. And how can he have repentance?'
By Allah! Even if he prostrates until his neck is cut off, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will not accept from him except through our Wilayah - the People of the Household.

Indeed! And whoever recognizes our rights and hopes for the reward in us, and is pleased with his sustenance of half a Mudd every day, and what covers his bareness, and what covers his head, and they, by Allah, are fearful and anxious in that. They wish that it is their share from the world.
And thus Allah, Mighty and Majestic, described them, saying: 'And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful, that they will return to their Lord.'

Then he said: 'What is that which they give? By Allah! They give with obedience, love, and Wilayah, and they are fearful in that. Their fear is not the fear of doubt, but they fear that they may be deficient in our love and our obedience.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the Household (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.نِصْفِ مُدٍّ: Half a Mudd (a measure of food)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for acceptance of worship according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi links the acceptance of worship to Wilayah, illustrating the Shia concept of 'Khawf al-Muhsinin' (fear of the righteous), where the pious are humble and fearful not of doubt, but of falling short in love for the Ahl al-Bayt. It contrasts the desire for fame with the spiritual benefit of obscurity, emphasizing that true merit lies in sincere devotion and contentment with provision. The narration underscores that obedience to the Imams is the essential key that validates all acts of worship.
